Set side length \(1\). Place
\[
A=(0,0),\quad B=(1,0).
\]
For convex \(ABCDE\), \(\angle A=90^\circ\) gives \(E=(0,1)\), and \(\angle B=90^\circ\) gives \(C=(1,1)\).

Then \(CE=1\). Since \(CD=DE=1\), triangle \(CDE\) is equilateral, so
\[
D=\left(\frac12,1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right).
\]
At \(E\),
\[
\overrightarrow{ED}=\left(\frac12,\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right),\qquad \overrightarrow{EA}=(0,-1).
\]
Thus
\[
\cos \angle E
=
\frac{\overrightarrow{ED}\cdot \overrightarrow{EA}}{|ED||EA|}
=
-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
So
\[
\angle E=150^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{150}
\]
